nodes.label: Pavement markings steer and regulate traffic like signs

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Markings as a class steer and regulate traffic like signs, while painted lane arrows specifically dictate which moves a lane allows or requires; learners think only signs carry rules.

nodes.label: White lines divide same-way lanes, yellow lines divide opposing traffic

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: White divides same-way lanes and yellow divides opposing traffic, and the contrast fact restates it as paint for traffic flowing together versus against each other; learners swap the colors.

nodes.label: White paint separates flow together, yellow paint flow against

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: White divides same-way lanes and yellow divides opposing traffic, and the contrast fact restates it as paint for traffic flowing together versus against each other; learners swap the colors.

nodes.label: Solid yellow side may not pass, dashed side may pass when safe

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Beside a solid yellow line you may not pass while the dashed side may, and the contrast fact restates it as holding your lane versus passing when safe; learners reverse the two sides.

nodes.label: Solid yellow holds your lane, its dashed twin lets you pass

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Beside a solid yellow line you may not pass while the dashed side may, and the contrast fact restates it as holding your lane versus passing when safe; learners reverse the two sides.

nodes.label: Yield lines are rows of white triangles marking where to yield

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Yield lines are white triangles marking where to yield, while the stop rule says to halt ahead of the stop line or crosswalk when a sign or signal demands a stop; learners confuse the yield point with the stop point.

nodes.label: Halt ahead of the stop line or crosswalk and give way to those crossing

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Yield lines are white triangles marking where to yield, while the stop rule says to halt ahead of the stop line or crosswalk when a sign or signal demands a stop; learners confuse the yield point with the stop point.

The stop rule says halt ahead of the stop line or crosswalk and give way, and the contrast fact separates the stop line that fixes where you halt from the crosswalk that fixes where pedestrians cross; learners treat them as one marking.

nodes.label: Stop line fixes the halt, crosswalk fixes the pedestrian crossing

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: The stop rule says halt ahead of the stop line or crosswalk and give way, and the contrast fact separates the stop line that fixes where you halt from the crosswalk that fixes where pedestrians cross; learners treat them as one marking.

nodes.label: Not every crosswalk is painted; stay alert at unmarked crossings

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Not every crosswalk is painted so you stay alert at unmarked crossings, and the contrast fact says painted crosswalks define the zone yet unpainted ones carry the same duty; learners drop the duty where paint is missing.

nodes.label: Painted crosswalks define the zone; unpainted carry the same duty

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Not every crosswalk is painted so you stay alert at unmarked crossings, and the contrast fact says painted crosswalks define the zone yet unpainted ones carry the same duty; learners drop the duty where paint is missing.

nodes.label: Painted lane arrows dictate which moves a lane allows or requires

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Markings as a class steer and regulate traffic like signs, while painted lane arrows specifically dictate which moves a lane allows or requires; learners think only signs carry rules.

Painted arrows dictate the moves a lane allows, while with no turn markings you start from the lane nearest your turn side and finish in the lane nearest your origin; learners apply the nearest-lane rule even where arrows say otherwise.

nodes.label: Reversible lanes flip by time of day; confirm the lane is yours

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Reversible lanes flip direction between double-dashed yellow lines, while the shared left-turn lane sits between solid-and-dashed yellow borders for waiting left turns; learners confuse the two center lanes.

nodes.label: Reversible signals: green opens, red X closes, flashing yellow turns only, steady yellow leave

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: The signal fact spells out all four reversible-lane signals, and the contrast fact pairs green with red and flashing yellow with steady yellow; learners swap the two yellow X meanings.

nodes.label: Green opens, red closes, flashing yellow narrows, steady yellow evicts

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: The signal fact spells out all four reversible-lane signals, and the contrast fact pairs green with red and flashing yellow with steady yellow; learners swap the two yellow X meanings.

nodes.label: Shared left-turn lane: enter and wait to turn, never pass

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Reversible lanes flip direction between double-dashed yellow lines, while the shared left-turn lane sits between solid-and-dashed yellow borders for waiting left turns; learners confuse the two center lanes.

The shared left-turn lane welcomes waiting left turns from both directions but never passing, and the contrast fact sets it against the reserved lane that admits only its posted vehicle class; learners treat both as open lanes.

nodes.label: Reserved lanes admit only posted vehicles, often marked by a white diamond

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: A reserved lane admits only the posted vehicle class, and the contrast fact pairs it with the shared left-turn lane that welcomes turns from both directions; learners enter the diamond lane as if it were a turn lane.

nodes.label: Shared turn lane welcomes turns, reserved lane admits one class

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: The shared left-turn lane welcomes waiting left turns from both directions but never passing, and the contrast fact sets it against the reserved lane that admits only its posted vehicle class; learners treat both as open lanes.

A reserved lane admits only the posted vehicle class, and the contrast fact pairs it with the shared left-turn lane that welcomes turns from both directions; learners enter the diamond lane as if it were a turn lane.

nodes.label: Left lane for passing; cruise right or center on three-plus lanes

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: The cruising fact keeps the left lane for passing and the right or center for cruising, and the contrast fact adds that the center lane serves heavy merging traffic; learners camp in the left lane.
The cruising fact gives the left lane to passing, while the contrast fact says the shoulder is never a travel or passing lane; learners treat the shoulder as an extra passing lane.

nodes.label: Never drive or pass on the shoulder unless sent there

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: The shoulder is off limits for driving or passing unless a device or official sends you there, and the contrast fact pairs it with the left lane that exists for passing; learners pass on the shoulder when the left lane is busy.

nodes.label: Shoulder never a travel lane, left lane exists for passing

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: The cruising fact gives the left lane to passing, while the contrast fact says the shoulder is never a travel or passing lane; learners treat the shoulder as an extra passing lane.

The shoulder is off limits for driving or passing unless a device or official sends you there, and the contrast fact pairs it with the left lane that exists for passing; learners pass on the shoulder when the left lane is busy.

nodes.label: Left lane passes, center lane serves heavy merging

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: The cruising fact keeps the left lane for passing and the right or center for cruising, and the contrast fact adds that the center lane serves heavy merging traffic; learners camp in the left lane.

nodes.label: No turn markings: nearest lane in, nearest lane out, shift only after

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Painted arrows dictate the moves a lane allows, while with no turn markings you start from the lane nearest your turn side and finish in the lane nearest your origin; learners apply the nearest-lane rule even where arrows say otherwise.

nodes.label: Bike lanes: solid white lines with bike symbols, sometimes separated

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Bike lanes are marked by solid white lines with bike symbols and grant exclusive space, and the contrast fact says sharrows merely announce sharing; learners read a sharrow as a bike lane.

nodes.label: Green bike lane: scan for cyclists before crossing, never stop on it

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Green lane paint warns drivers to scan before crossing and never stop on it, and the contrast fact separates it from the green bike box that gives cyclists a turning pocket at signals; learners confuse the two green markings.

nodes.label: Drivers cross a bike lane only to turn, checking alongside and behind

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Drivers may enter a bike lane only to turn with careful checks, and the contrast fact pairs that with cyclists using detector marks to trigger signals; learners assume the bike lane is open to cars when empty.

nodes.label: Sharrows announce sharing and reserve no exclusive space

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Sharrows warn that bikes share the lane but reserve no exclusive space, and the contrast fact says bike lanes do grant exclusive marked space; learners expect cars to stay out of a sharrow lane.

nodes.label: Bike lanes grant exclusive space, sharrows only announce sharing

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Bike lanes are marked by solid white lines with bike symbols and grant exclusive space, and the contrast fact says sharrows merely announce sharing; learners read a sharrow as a bike lane.
Sharrows warn that bikes share the lane but reserve no exclusive space, and the contrast fact says bike lanes do grant exclusive marked space; learners expect cars to stay out of a sharrow lane.

nodes.label: Bike boxes: green full-width zones at signals giving cyclists a turning pocket

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: A bike box is a green full-width zone at signals giving cyclists a turning pocket, and the contrast fact says plain green lane paint only warns drivers crossing it; learners stop in the box as if it were a lane.

nodes.label: A pavement detector mark shows cyclists where to trip the signal

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: The detector mark shows cyclists where to trip the signal, and the contrast fact pairs it with the rule that motorists enter bike lanes only to turn; learners read the mark as a stop point for cars.

nodes.label: Green lane paint warns drivers, green bike box pockets cyclists

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Green lane paint warns drivers to scan before crossing and never stop on it, and the contrast fact separates it from the green bike box that gives cyclists a turning pocket at signals; learners confuse the two green markings.

nodes.label: Motorists enter bike lanes only to turn; cyclists use detector marks

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Drivers may enter a bike lane only to turn with careful checks, and the contrast fact pairs that with cyclists using detector marks to trigger signals; learners assume the bike lane is open to cars when empty.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: start with markings as regulators, then white versus yellow lines, solid versus dashed yellow, yield lines, stop lines and crosswalks painted or not

curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on what each line color and marking requires

curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: one-fact cards on cruising lanes, the shoulder, the two contrasts and the turn-path rule
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on which lane to cruise, pass or turn from and when the shoulder is off limits

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: teach how bike lanes are marked, green paint, crossing only to turn, sharrows, bike boxes and detector marks, then the three bicycle contrasts

curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on what each bicycle marking means and when a driver may cross a bike lane
